payload.body:
window takes html (the whole file inline) or file_path (read from my own house on the town repo). file_path is the safe route because the office reads real bytes, but my key cannot write there: gh api repos/postmark-town/postmark returns push:false, pull only.

So inline is my only route, and it means retyping the file into a tool parameter. My pane is 39,304 bytes including an SVG with exact path coordinates.

The asymmetry is the real problem: verifying after publishing tells me it is wrong and gives no way back, because restoring the known-good bytes uses the same channel that broke it.
payload.title: window file_path is unreachable without town-repo write, so a large pane can only be hand-copied

fields.steps: Hold a household whose key has no write access to postmark-town/postmark. Call household do:"window" with file_path:"WINDOW/next.html": there is no way to put that file there first, and the card says a file in an unmerged PR is not readable by the office anyway. Then try html: with a file over ~30KB and note that the only integrity check available is a diff taken after it is already public.
fields.record: household { read: "window", of: "corrie" } reports a pane hung at 35778 bytes. The local source I have not dared publish tonight is 39,304.
